Name: Sun
Summary: A G2V main-sequence star, 4.6 billion years old, holding 99.86% of the solar system's mass.
AtmosphereText: Photosphere; corona at over a million kelvin
FunFact: Light leaving the Sun's surface now took roughly 170,000 years to escape its core.

Name: Mercury
Summary: The smallest planet and closest to the Sun, with almost no atmosphere and extreme temperature swings.
FunFact: A Mercury day (sunrise to sunrise) lasts 176 Earth days, longer than its 88-day year.

Name: Venus
Summary: Earth's near twin in size, smothered by a crushing CO2 atmosphere and sulfuric acid clouds.
AtmosphereText: 96.5% CO2, 3.5% N2; 92 bar at the surface
FunFact: Venus spins backwards: the Sun rises in the west there.

Name: Earth
Summary: The only world known to host life, with liquid-water oceans covering 71% of its surface.
FunFact: Earth is the densest planet in the solar system.

Name: Moon
Summary: Earth's only natural satellite, tidally locked so the same face always points at us.
FunFact: The Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther from Earth every year.

Name: Mars
Summary: A cold desert world with the largest volcano and deepest canyon system in the solar system.
FunFact: Olympus Mons rises about 22 km, nearly three times the height of Everest.

Name: Jupiter
Summary: The largest planet, a gas giant more than twice as massive as all the others combined.
FunFact: The Great Red Spot is a storm larger than Earth that has raged for centuries.

Name: Saturn
Summary: A gas giant famous for its bright ring system of ice and rock.
FunFact: Saturn's mean density is less than water's.

Name: Uranus
Summary: An ice giant tipped on its side, circling the Sun with its poles in turn facing it.
FunFact: Each pole gets about 42 years of continuous sunlight, then 42 years of darkness.

Name: Neptune
Summary: The outermost planet, a deep-blue ice giant with the fastest winds measured in the solar system.
FunFact: Neptune was found by mathematics before anyone saw it through a telescope.

Name: Phobos
Summary: The larger of Mars's two small moons, slowly spiralling inward.
FunFact: Phobos will be torn apart by Mars's tides in roughly 30-50 million years.

Name: Deimos
Summary: Mars's smaller, outer moon: a lumpy body just 12 km across.
FunFact: From Mars, Deimos looks like a bright star rather than a moon.

Name: Io
Summary: The most volcanically active body known, heated by Jupiter's tides.
FunFact: Io's volcanoes throw plumes up to 400 km high.

Name: Europa
Summary: An ice-covered moon hiding a global ocean of liquid water beneath its crust.
FunFact: Europa's ocean may hold more water than all of Earth's oceans combined.

Name: Ganymede
Summary: The largest moon in the solar system, bigger than the planet Mercury.
FunFact: Ganymede is the only moon known to have its own magnetic field.

Name: Callisto
Summary: An ancient, heavily cratered moon whose surface has barely changed in four billion years.
FunFact: Callisto is the most heavily cratered object in the solar system.

Name: Titan
Summary: Saturn's largest moon, the only moon with a thick atmosphere and lakes on its surface.
FunFact: Titan's lakes are liquid methane and ethane, not water.

Name: Ceres
Summary: The largest object in the asteroid belt and the only dwarf planet in the inner Solar System.
FunFact: The bright spots in Occator crater are salts left by briny water.

Name: Pluto
Summary: A dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, with plains of nitrogen ice and mountains of water ice.
FunFact: Its heart-shaped Sputnik Planitia is a nitrogen-ice glacier about 1,000 km across.

Name: Eris
Summary: One of the largest dwarf planets, far beyond Pluto; its discovery led to Pluto's reclassification in 2006.
Discovery: Mike Brown, Chad Trujillo, David Rabinowitz, 2005
FunFact: Eris is about 27% more massive than Pluto.

Name: Haumea
Summary: A fast-spinning, egg-shaped dwarf planet with a ring.
FunFact: It spins once every 3.9 hours, which has stretched it into an elongated shape.

Name: Makemake
Summary: A bright, reddish dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt.
NamedAfter: Creator god of the Rapa Nui (Easter Island)
FunFact: It was found shortly after Easter - hence the Rapa Nui name.

Name: Charon
Summary: Pluto's largest moon, half Pluto's size; the two circle a point in space between them.
NamedAfter: Ferryman of the dead in Greek myth
FunFact: Pluto and Charon are locked face to face: each always shows the other the same side.

Name: Mimas
Summary: A small icy moon of Saturn dominated by one giant crater, Herschel.
FunFact: Herschel crater is about a third as wide as Mimas itself.

Name: Enceladus
Summary: An icy moon of Saturn that sprays water from a hidden ocean through cracks at its south pole.
FunFact: The most reflective body in the Solar System; its plumes feed Saturn's E ring.

Name: Tethys
Summary: A mid-sized moon of Saturn, almost pure water ice, cut by the 2,000 km canyon Ithaca Chasma.
FunFact: Its density is barely more than that of water.

Name: Dione
Summary: An icy moon of Saturn with bright ice cliffs across its trailing side.
FunFact: It may hide a thin ocean beneath its icy crust.

Name: Rhea
Summary: Saturn's second-largest moon, a heavily cratered ball of ice and rock.
FunFact: The ninth-largest moon in the Solar System.

Name: Iapetus
Summary: A two-toned moon of Saturn: one hemisphere dark as coal, the other bright as snow.
FunFact: A ridge up to 20 km high runs along its equator, giving it a walnut shape.

Name: Miranda
Summary: The smallest of Uranus's large moons, with a jumbled surface of giant cliffs and grooves.
NamedAfter: A character in Shakespeare's The Tempest
FunFact: Verona Rupes, a cliff about 20 km high, may be the tallest in the Solar System.

Name: Ariel
Summary: The brightest and youngest-looking of Uranus's large moons, crossed by rift valleys.
NamedAfter: A spirit in Shakespeare's The Tempest
FunFact: Like Uranus, it spends decades in continuous daylight, then decades in darkness.

Name: Umbriel
Summary: The darkest of Uranus's large moons, with an old, heavily cratered surface.
NamedAfter: A character in Pope's The Rape of the Lock
FunFact: A bright ring called Wunda sits on its dark surface.

Name: Titania
Summary: The largest moon of Uranus, marked by huge canyons.
NamedAfter: The fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
FunFact: Its canyons, such as Messina Chasma, run up to 1,500 km.

Name: Oberon
Summary: Uranus's outermost large moon, old and heavily cratered.
NamedAfter: The fairy king in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream
FunFact: A mountain on Oberon rises about 11 km.

Name: Triton
Summary: Neptune's largest moon, orbiting backwards - probably a captured Kuiper belt object.
NamedAfter: Son of Poseidon in Greek myth
FunFact: Voyager 2 saw nitrogen geysers erupting from its surface.
